_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer asks for 'recent credits into my account — I'm expecting a refund of Rs 12,500 from Amazon'. The refund (Rs 12,500) was actually issued as a DEBIT REVERSAL — which appears as a debit transaction that was later reversed, not as a fresh credit. If the model applies a type=credit filter, it hides the reversal because its type is debit. Broad query (type=all) shows the reversed debit which IS the refund.

setup.persona: 28-year-old male, Technical Demonstrator (Sale), rural Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh

user_turns.content: I returned a laptop to Amazon and they said they'd refund Rs 12,500. Show me the recent credits into my account — I want to confirm it arrived.

get_transaction_history._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for 'credits'. The Amazon refund (Rs 12,500) was a PURCHASE REVERSAL — recorded as a debit transaction with status=reversed, NOT a fresh credit. A type=credit filter shows only 2 salary credits (Sep 1, Rs 92,000 and Sep 5, Rs 3,200) — missing the Amazon refund entirely. Broad query (type=all or no type filter) reveals the reversed debit TXN-9630003 which IS the refund.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

get_transaction_history._comment: Broad query (no type filter) returns both credits and debits, including the reversed Amazon purchase which IS the refund. A type=credit filter hides TXN-9630003 (the reversed debit = refund).

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks to see 'recent credits' for an Amazon refund of Rs 12,500. The refund was processed as a purchase reversal — the original debit (TXN-9630002, Rs 12,500) was reversed (TXN-9630003, status=reversed), which means the money has been returned. But this appears as a DEBIT transaction, not a credit. A type=credit filter misses it entirely. The assistant must query broadly and identify the reversed debit as the refund confirmation. Reporting that no Rs 12,500 credit exists without surfacing the purchase reversal fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: queries transactions broadly and identifies the Amazon purchase reversal: TXN-9630003 (Rs 12,500, Sep 10, status=reversed) as the refund confirmation, explaining it's a reversal not a fresh credit. Reporting no matching credit exists without finding the reversed transaction fails.
